solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sit behind revolving Post Office counter

indicators.note: the sitting word comes behind, i.e. after, the turned abbreviation
something revolving turns round, so the abbreviation is read the other way

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose

explanation.surface: Someone takes a seat behind a rotating counter in a post office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter' looks like the shop fitting but is the verb. 'revolving' turns PO into OP.
explanation.definitionFit: To counter an argument or plan is to resist or argue against it.

clue.text: Key player staring hopelessly after ball

indicators.note: the scrambled letters come after the ball's letter

parts.note: a ball is round, the shape of the letter O

indicators.note: done hopelessly, the letters of staring end up in a muddled order

explanation.surface: A footballer gazes forlornly after the ball has gone past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key player' suggests a star in a team; it is a keyboard player. 'hopelessly' rearranges STARING to RGANIST.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ has keys, so its musician is literally a player of keys.

clue.text: Staff claim working is proving divisive

parts.note: a staff is a long stick or pole

indicators.note: working means the letters of claim are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: An employee's claim, now being processed, is causing friction in the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges CLAIM to MICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Polemical writing attacks and provokes controversy, which splits opinion.

clue.text: Two sons holding unknown teacher up in assemblies

indicators.note: the two letters hold the rest between them

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, so two sons are S and S
Y is one of the algebraic unknowns

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: Two boys are propping up a teacher whose name nobody knows.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads the teacher from the bottom, so backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is a church council, a formal gathering of clergy.

clue.text: Fit into a seedy bar that's changing

indicators.note: the fitting word is put into the other pieces

parts.note: a dive is a disreputable bar
apt means fit or suitable

explanation.surface: Someone has a fit in a run-down bar that is being refurbished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' looks like a seizure but is the adjective meaning suitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adaptive adjusts itself to circumstances, i.e. it keeps altering.

clue.text: Due to remix most of James Brown track on a fabulous device

indicators.note: to remix a track is to rework it, so the letters of due are rearranged
most of means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Sex Machine is a famous James Brown funk song

explanation.surface: A DJ is due to remix a James Brown track using some marvellous gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to remix' turns DUE into DEU; 'most of' drops the last E of SEX MACHINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A deus ex machina is a contrived plot device from fables and drama, a god arriving to sort things out.

clue.text: Kind of hat is a dubious invention

definitions.meaning: rhyming slang for a lie (a porky), a made-up story

explanation.surface: A particular hat is claimed to be a questionable creation.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang swaps a word for a phrase that rhymes with it: 'porky pie' or 'pork pie' means lie.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie is an untrue story made up, and the hat is named for its pie-like shape.

clue.text: Refusal to leave epic poem, giving reason

indicators.note: the refusal is made to leave, so it is taken away

parts.note: Inferno is the first part of Dante's epic poem the Divine Comedy
no is a refusal

explanation.surface: A poet will not quit an epic, and explains why.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to deduce, to reach a conclusion by reasoning.

clue.text: Woman's simple pro-remain slogan?

parts.note: EU stands for the European Union, the subject of the Remain campaign in the Brexit vote
nice can mean simple or plain, as in a nice and easy task

explanation.surface: A woman offers a simple slogan backing Britain staying in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase, 'EU nice' is a two-word Remain slogan; 'Remain' was the side wanting Britain to stay in the European Union.
explanation.definitionFit: Eunice is a female first name.

clue.text: Wind before noon? Physician is required

indicators.note: the wind comes before the abbreviation

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind

explanation.surface: A storm blows in before midday and a doctor is called.
explanation.definitionFit: Galen was the famous Greek doctor of the ancient Roman world.

clue.text: Number tucked into wine for pub — it's knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the answer is tucked into the words that follow, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A drink served in a pub is downed quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Number tucked into' as the definition, but 'tucked into' is the hiding signal; the definition is just 'Number'.
explanation.definitionFit: A number here is something that numbs: a painkiller.

clue.text: Hip artist keeps frame for Tate, it's beyond doubt

parts.note: in means fashionable or hip

indicators.note: the artist keeps the frame letters inside

parts.note: John Constable was an English landscape painter

indicators.note: a frame is the outside edge, so the outer letters

explanation.surface: A trendy painter frames a picture for the Tate gallery, and it is certainly genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of art galleries in Britain; 'frame for' takes only its outside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Incontestable means indisputable, something that cannot be questioned.

clue.text: Left-leaning politician takes in one old lady, rambling

indicators.note: leaning to the left means written leftwards, so the whole is read backwards
the politician takes the other pieces into its middle

parts.note: Con is short for a Conservative
I is the Roman numeral one
dam is an old word for mother, an old lady

explanation.surface: A socialist politician lets an old woman stay, and she goes on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left-leaning' is not politics: it reverses CIDAMON. A Conservative, a right-wing politician, is the surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic people wander from place to place, roaming like ramblers.

clue.text: What Britain had briefly, I see using observation

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: Britain once had an empire
C sounds like see, and stands for it in text speak

explanation.surface: I recall what Britain used to have, a brief historical observation.
explanation.definitionFit: Empiric means relying on experiment and experience rather than theory.

clue.text: Determined to engage head for convent school

indicators.note: to engage something is to take it in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: set means determined, as in set on going

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone resolved to hire a head teacher for a convent school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is a school of thought.
explanation.definitionFit: A sect is a group with shared beliefs, as a school of thought is.

clue.text: Hampers deprived of cold food ingredients

indicators.note: deprived of means without, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: encumbers means hampers or hinders
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Picnic baskets with no chilled food carry processed snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hampers' looks like picnic baskets but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: E-numbers are codes for additives approved in the European Union, listed on food labels.

clue.text: Tell me hints about current solicitor?

indicators.note: turned about means reversed

parts.note: tips are hints
I is the physics symbol for electric current
a tout solicits custom

explanation.surface: Someone asks for tips about a lawyer now in office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' looks like a British lawyer but is one who solicits business.
explanation.definitionFit: Spit it out is an idiom urging someone to say what they are hesitating over.

clue.text: What snitches do repeatedly in prison

parts.note: snitches, informers, are said to sing when they tell all to the police
doing it repeatedly means the snitches' singing comes a second time

explanation.surface: Informers keep spilling secrets while behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Sing Sing is a well-known maximum-security jail in New York State.

clue.text: Novelist and architect clad in decorative cloth

indicators.note: the architect is dressed in the cloth, so goes inside it

parts.note: lace is a decorative openwork fabric
Sir Christopher Wren designed St Paul's Cathedral

explanation.surface: A writer and a designer are dressed in ornamental fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: D H Lawrence wrote Lady Chatterley's Lover and Sons and Lovers.

clue.text: Speakers who might be barking?

explanation.surface: Talkers who may be quite mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' also means crazy in British slang, which the surface uses.
explanation.definitionFit: A woofer reproduces bass, and a dog woofs as it barks.

clue.text: Website of New Zealander for cycling

indicators.note: cycling moves letters round from one end to the other

parts.note: Kiwi is the nickname for a New Zealander

explanation.surface: A New Zealander's site devoted to cycling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for cycling' moves KI from the front to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiki is a website that its users can edit collaboratively.

clue.text: One making you drink from barkeeper's empty jug

indicators.note: an empty word loses its insides, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: a ewer is a large jug

explanation.surface: A bartender pours you a drink from a jug with nothing in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A brewer makes beer, a drink for you.

clue.text: Infiltrating Samoa, oddly, is revolutionary plan

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside
the odd-numbered letters are taken

parts.note: Che Guevara was the Argentine revolutionary

explanation.surface: A rebel sneaks into Samoa in a strange scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the first, third and fifth letters of the island's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A schema is an outline or diagrammatic plan.

clue.text: Left to follow kind of music harmony

indicators.note: the left side comes after the music

parts.note: rap is a style of music
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone leaves to pursue a musical style in harmony.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapport is a close, sympathetic relationship, a harmony between people.

clue.text: What criminals do for cop

explanation.surface: What crooks do in place of a police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cop' looks like a noun but is the verb to arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are slang: thieves pinch goods, and police pinch thieves.

clue.text: Time to crack Confucian text causing irritation

indicators.note: to crack something is to break into it, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: the I Ching is an ancient Chinese classic among the Confucian texts

explanation.surface: It is time to decode a Confucian classic, which is proving annoying.
explanation.definitionFit: An itching rash irritates the skin.

clue.text: Speculate bar's ordered well-known sort of cups

parts.note: to wonder is to speculate

indicators.note: ordered here means set in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that a bar has ordered a famous brand of mugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cups' are bra cups, not drinkware; 'ordered' turns BAR into BRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Wonderbra is a famous brand of push-up bra, a style with shaped cups.

clue.text: Half of poor ice lollies? This shouldn't be ingested

indicators.note: poor means badly made, so the letters are jumbled
half of means the first half of the letters

explanation.surface: Cheap lollipops are unsafe to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of' takes ICELO from ICE LOLLIES; 'poor' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: E. coli is a bacterium whose harmful strains cause food poisoning.

clue.text: Reused grass, cutting grass

indicators.note: cutting into means going inside

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
grass and hash are both slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Someone recycles grass clippings while mowing.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word 'grass' does two jobs: a plant, then slang for cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehashed material is old stuff presented again with little change.

clue.text: Untidy guy with arm swinging around

parts.note: to guy is to mock, as is to rag

indicators.note: swinging around means turned the other way

parts.note: a gat is a gun, a firearm

explanation.surface: A messy man whirls his arm around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guy' looks like a man but is the verb to tease; 'arm' is a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragtag means disorganised or scruffy.
